To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

recombinant TNFs do not inhibit the growth in vitro of African trypanosome strains that cause lethal infections in mice, and that the TNF gene disruption in mice increases the parasitemia and the lethality of infections with these trypanosomes.
recombinant TNFs do not inhibit trypanosome growth in axenic culture and that the effects of TNFs on trypanosome infections are likely to be indirect.

recombinant mouse TNF- α inhibits the growth of two African trypanosomes in vitro but that human TNF- α does not inhibit the in vitro growth of any of four African trypanosomes and that the in vivo effects of recombinants of TNF- α on African trypanosome infections may be indirect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of TNF- α on African trypanosomes and its role as an antitrypanosomal agent.
the effect of recombinant tumor necrosis factor (TNF) alpha on the growth of African Trypanosoma species.
the role of TNF- α as an immunomodulator in the pathogenesis of human trypanosomiasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

recombinant mouse TNF- α, human TNF- α or bovine TNF α do not inhibit the growth and development of African trypanosome in axenic culture conditions, and therefore the effect on parasitemia observed in mice is most likely indirect.
recombinant TNFa does not inhibit the in vitro growth of any of these African trypanosomes and, in addition, does not inhibit the development of T. br. brucei GUGat3.1 in mice.
recombinant TNFa does not affect the growth and survival of African trypanosome isolates under axenic culture condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth of trypanosomes is not inhibited by recombinant TNFs in axenic cultures.

TNF-α is a cytokine that has been reported to be produced by mice and humans in response to trypanosome infection, but it does not appear to be directly involved in the growth of the trypanosomes in vitro.
TNF-α is not a trypanocidal agent, and that TNF- α does not inhibit trypanosome growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of TNF- α on trypanosomes are not straightforward and may vary with the strain of trypanosome used.
recombinant TNFs do not kill bloodstream-form trypanosomes under axenic culture.
the use of recombinant murine, human, or bovine TNF-alpha to inhibit trypanosome growth in vitro is likely to be of limited utility.
